name: Muhammad Shia' al-Sudani
role: Iraqi prime minister (2022–2026) and Reconstruction and Development Coalition leader
summary: Al-Sudani advocates development led by public infrastructure investment and greater private-sector participation, with poverty reduction and institutional reform among his stated priorities. He pairs climate-transition commitments with expanded oil and gas development, supports capital punishment for drug offences and favours state control of weapons through negotiated disarmament linked to sovereignty.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He told the UN that occupation, annexation and redrawing borders by force contradict international resolutions, citing Resolutions 242 and others.

death-penalty.rationale: He explicitly asks the president to ratify all final death sentences in drug cases as deterrence and enforcement of the law.

decide-locally.rationale: He explicitly proposes strengthening local governments’ capabilities and effectiveness within a federal democratic system.

democracy-best.rationale: He expressly credits belief in democracy with closing Iraq’s chapter of conflict and endorses open dialogue as a governing principle.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His UN speech calls Iraq’s diversity one of its most valuable assets and prioritises protecting minority communities.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He jointly commits to ending associated-gas flaring by 2028 and expands climate and energy-transition cooperation with the UK.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He criticises Security Council powerlessness and calls on international institutions to fulfil their peacekeeping and protection responsibilities.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He seeks a larger OPEC export quota and expressly welcomes companies investing in Iraqi oil and gas development.

future-generations.rationale: He connects international environmental cooperation and sustainable water management with building a better future for coming generations.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: He announced the creation of a Higher Council for Women's Affairs to handle women's development decisions.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He advocates a national anti-drug strategy, coercive enforcement and stronger counter-narcotics capacity, while also supporting treatment of users.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He supports constitutional federal partnership with the Kurdistan Regional Government based on recognised rights and duties.

more-religion-public.rationale: He explicitly calls for using religious and social guidance as part of the national effort against drugs.

nation-first.rationale: He explicitly describes his policy as Iraq First, placing Iraqi interests at the forefront while maintaining international engagement.

national-self-determination.rationale: He affirms self-determination and says Palestinians should enjoy a state like other peoples.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: From 2024 he sought a negotiated end to the coalition's presence as destabilising, and by January 2026 announced he had fully taken over Ain al-Asad base and the Harir mission would end; he earlier (2023) said he was not opposed to US troops, and keeps bilateral counterterrorism cooperation.

one-party-rule.rationale: His formation speech promises openness to all political forces, including those outside the government, rather than exclusive party rule.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He presented his government as including all Iraqi sects and components as the basis of consensus and stability.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His government-formation speech makes combating poverty, unemployment and empowering low-income people central economic priorities.

refugee-return.rationale: His government made displaced persons and refugees a priority and sought their voluntary and safe return to their original homes.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He told the UN that incitement and hatred must be distinguished from free expression, called Quran burning a hate crime, and urged international cooperation against hate speech.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He advocates reforming the international economic system and closing North–South technological gaps through Iraq’s G77 role.

separated-powers.rationale: His programme expressly guarantees judicial independence under the constitution, supporting a judiciary separate from executive control.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His August 2026 statement endorses negotiated state control of weapons, linked to coalition withdrawal, ending drone flights and foreign airspace violations.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He promotes the Development Road network of railways, highways, industrial cities and the Al-Faw port as a state-led development priority.

state-harmful.rationale: Building state institutions and asserting the rule of law are stated priorities of his government, which contradicts the view that the state is harmful.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He said Iraq will not follow a policy of polarization and will deal with everyone by national interest, with an independent and balanced foreign policy.

notes:
Reviewed all 490 statements against the full downloaded 2024 UN speech, his government-formation speech, the 2025 UK joint statement and later statements through August 2026. Former prime-minister status verified rather than assumed current. No view is inferred from his party, sect or alliance with other politicians. Parliament’s 2024 same-sex criminalisation and 2025 personal-status changes are not automatically attributed as personal endorsements without evidence of his own position. IDP return advocacy is not expanded into an explicit position on descendants’ refugee-return rights. Digital government is not algorithmic rule. Ending the coalition combat mission does not imply ending every military partnership: his January 2026 statement expressly retains coalition counterterrorism cooperation. His latest disarmament statement links sequencing to foreign withdrawal and airspace sovereignty. The Arabic state-agency drug speech is dated 9 December 2023, whereas the HRW article describes its linked statement as September; the primary text and its displayed date control here. Evidence of treatment for drug dependency is not a documented position on the overarching purpose of prisons.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 8 answers taken from it, 16 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Themes searched: economy, government, world, liberty, society, ecology, from his two UN speeches, the programme speech, April 2025 remarks, Reuters/Arab News/WSJ-era interviews on the coalition, the Arabic drug-offence speech, UK joint statement, January 2026 weapons statement and the personal status law episode. The 2024-25 personal status amendments and the same-sex criminalisation law were passed by parliament; no statement of his own endorsing them was found, so they are null. Pmo.iq returned 404 and 964media returned 403 directly; the latter was read from a Wayback capture. The Commons Library page returned 403 and was read via Wayback. Answers on armed-forces, state-investment and Kurdistan rest partly on his programme speech as reported, not full text. Government acts count only where he spoke for them.
